480	but for one thing. What is the thing that the Holy One, blessed be He, created
the world for? That a person merit to be a giver. The Holy
Blessed One is only a giver. Heaven forbid, He takes
nothing. He needs nothing from anyone
in the world. What does the Holy One do? Only give.
Give, give and give, give and give.
And whoever merits to cleave to His attributes,
to give and give, that is the purpose of Creation. For this
the Holy One created the world, "and to cleave to
Him," to cleave to the deeds of the Creator, who only
gives. That is how a person must merit to live. Uh, we,
sometimes when you receive, you worry: what for, what for
what are they giving me? I need to give, I myself, I
myself,
that is the merit. A proven segulah, a mitzvah, tested:
finding a match, children, everything. Go out from his service
and come to give thanks for the visit to the grave of the Or HaChaim
HaKadosh. Many people. One
man
took, he had three children, he tells it himself,
he told.
Three children, two sons and a daughter, who needed to marry,
and already grown, aged 28,
30, and the girl 27. This
man, they told him to take stones, place them on the grave of
the Or HaChaim HaKadosh, and afterwards take them.
He took three stones at the grave of the Or HaChaim HaKadosh,
he took them
for his three children. This is a story of a relative
who did this thing.
That same year two of them
got married and one the following year,
the same year.
The segulot of the Or HaChaim HaKadosh are truly wondrous,
extraordinary.
And the segulot for health, for healing, cannot be
described, cannot be described. Well, there was a holy
Admor
who had come to him,
a man who had been told something about his eyes,
that his eyes
were growing dim, truly growing dim, growing dim,
he had almost,
Heaven forbid, stopped seeing, barely
at all.
He went to a holy Admor.
He said to him:
Take this passage of the Or HaChaim,
whichever passage, learn it every day, and you will see. Go
and pray at the grave of the Or HaChaim HaKadosh and learn
this passage of the Or HaChaim HaKadosh.
Good.
He went
to the grave of the Or HaChaim HaKadosh, pleaded, wept,
and afterwards began to learn the passage. After about
a month of learning this passage,
his eyes were opened.
After his eyes were opened,
someone, apparently, poor fellow, somebody,
looks for this passage and does not find it.
He does not know, does not remember. Every day he would say
this passage, and suddenly it was gone. He does not
search in the Chumash, maybe here, maybe there, he does not
see it.
He went to the Admor.
He said to him: That is what I had at that time. Now
I too do not know, but I tell you,
listen,
this is how one must learn all of the Or HaChaim HaKadosh. Perhaps
you will meet it, perhaps it is that same person who needs to meet
this passage.
That is to say, the Or HaChaim HaKadosh planted within
his books a kind of supernal holiness
of match, of health, of children,
of long, good days,
rectified, of livelihood too. Many people.
One tells that he was about to go bankrupt, truly had no
way out. He was told: go to the Or
HaChaim HaKadosh, pray from the depths of the heart, weep there. He went
two, three hours, finished all of Tehilim in tears, and suddenly
things went up. He did not go bankrupt. On the contrary, the opposite, he became
and he himself became one of the supporters of
Torah. All this [snorts] in the merit of
our master the tzaddik, that we merited.
This is a merit, we think, and
with great emotion, he saw.
Wow, a number of healing segulot, all of them proven,
proven.
Do you hear, proven, his healing segulot.
Ay.
There was the holy
Rabbi Aharon of Belz.
He is a supreme holy man, holy of holies, one of the survivors
of the Holocaust. They brought him, they saved him, they brought him.
He was in the Holy Land, everyone knew. I told you
once.
It was the Sinai war. In the Sinai war there was
danger to life. They dug pits, trenches, caves, places
to be, because there were not even shelters.
The Egyptians received
advanced planes from Russia. They bought from Russia, and other
countries, advanced planes. And these planes
were meant to enter and bring devastation
upon Israel.
And they did not know what to do.
The tzaddik of Belz
was told that this war was to begin on
Tuesday. Tuesday.
Tuesday. That is, Tuesday evening, the war,
Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
Three days.
They tell, all his Chassidim, that he stood by the
window, held his hand up like this, three days,
until Shabbat morning.
Until Shabbat morning he did not pray, did not put on
tefilin, nothing, he stood like this,
with his hand like this, truly.
"And do the hands of Moshe make war or break
war? Rather, when Israel look upward and subjugate
their hearts to their Father in heaven," he stood like that.
